layout_sources: https://github.com/deb-sig/double-entry-generator/blob/master/example/bmo/credit/example-bmo-records.csv (preamble line, Item #,Card #,Transaction Date,Posting Date,Transaction Amount,Description; apostrophe-wrapped card number; YYYYMMDD; amounts like 6.0)
https://github.com/deb-sig/double-entry-generator/blob/master/pkg/provider/bmo/util.go (credit card: an amount starting with "-" is money received, anything else a purchase)
notes: Same preamble as BMO's chequing download ("Following data is valid as of ... (Year/Month/Day/Hour/Minute/Second)"); the one card sample has an edited first line and a single blank line, so the two blank lines either side of the header are assumed from the chequing file. Header Item #,Card #,Transaction Date,Posting Date,Transaction Amount,Description. Item # counts from 1; Card # in apostrophes; both dates YYYYMMDD (expect.json uses the transaction date). Purchases positive, payments and refunds negative, as BMO sees the card; written as floats without trailing zeros (1268.4, -1500.0), no thousands separator. Oldest first. No balance. CRLF and the file name are assumed.
